key_insight: Light can reversibly swap halide ions in 2D mixed-halide perovskites through strong light-lattice coupling, not defects, enabling defect-free photo-switching with self-resetting behavior in the dark.
engineering_relevance: This points to a new route for tunable, reversible optoelectronic devices and photoresponsive solar-cell materials that can switch optical properties on demand without permanent degradation.
method: Nudged elastic band calculations mapped the halide-exchange energy pathway and activation barrier.
Photo-force calculations showed that illumination does non-equilibrium work to drive partial halide motion.
Lattice dynamics and GW optics were used to identify soft modes, band-edge electron-phonon coupling, and light-induced bandgap renormalization.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports agreement with experimentally observed absorption spectra in the dark and a clear illumination-induced redshift consistent with light-driven bandgap renormalization.
watch_item: The mechanism depends on a delicate light-lattice interaction that only partially overcomes the exchange barrier, so device performance may be sensitive to illumination conditions and material stability.
paper_title: Reversible photo-switching optical functionality in two-dimensional mixed-halide hybrid perovskites
